items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: And I had the best studio, a guy named Dan Wallin in the Burbank Studio, this was the top soundstage.

ctx.x: No kidding. I would have been very anxious going in front of a symphony orchestra of L.A. musicians, being it was the first time that you’d done that.

Well what I did is I was realistic. I amassed a wonderful team. And here I have to really thank Roger Kellaway, who had been doing movie scores for a number of years down there, and I called Roger and I said, “look I’ve got this opportunity, I don’t know a damn thing about how Hollywood works with this stuff, who do I need here?” So it ended up Roger conducted the orchestra for me, because I’d had no experience conducting at all, I got Greg McRitchie to do the orchestration, because he was a seasoned orchestrator…

trumpets be playing this same note an octave higher? He was a master orchestrator. Did a beautiful job. And I had a top musical editor who prepared the timing sheets for me so I knew just exactly to a tenth of a second how much music was needed in every scene. And a top contractor. So I had a super, super team, the best LA musicians, because again Roger told me all the guys to hire.
